## Simon Willison from Simon Willison’s Newsletter — Datasette Agent: an AI assistant for Datasette built on LLM

_From: `[email]` · 2026-05-22T06:45:47+00:00_

View this post on the web at https://simonw.substack.com/p/datasette-agent-an-ai-assistant-for

In this newsletter:
Datasette Agent
Gemini 3.5 Flash: more expensive, but Google plan to use it for everything
Plus 2 links and 1 quotation and 1 note and 3 beats
Thanks for reading Simon Willison’s Newsletter! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
Sponsor message: exe.dev [ https://substack.com/redirect/57768c25-a736-493b-8e2a-0bfea31ea868?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] runs persistent VMs for the agent era. SSH and root, plus HTTPS and auth out of the box. Secrets injected at the network edge stay out of the LLM's hands. Run agents, internal tools, side projects, whatever. It's just a computer.
Datasette Agent [ https://substack.com/redirect/5a946a9d-1599-4246-9252-e1e2da8b58b1?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] - 2026-05-21
We just announced the first release of Datasette Agent [ https://substack.com/redirect/31979d87-997a-44ae-bf95-fad7283ac7cb?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ], a new extensible AI assistant for Datasette. I’ve been working on my LLM [ https://substack.com/redirect/02b0359d-ca15-4ab3-a3b7-a03c223e4281?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] Python library for just over three years now, and Datasette Agent represents the moment that LLM and Datasette [ https://substack.com/redirect/404bd75a-e40a-43fa-a741-2c427cb92a37?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] finally come together. I’m really excited about it!
Datasette Agent provides a conversational interface for asking questions of the data you have stored in Datasette. Add the datasette-agent-charts [ https://substack.com/redirect/a3b3e3cd-807f-4040-bc65-be2a2fd6142e?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] plugin and it can generate charts of your data as well.
The demo
The announcement post [ https://substack.com/redirect/d02c9825-a7fc-40eb-acc1-e2f2ed05a228?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] (on the new Datasette project blog) includes this demo video [ https://substack.com/redirect/145668bd-77cd-47e9-8ef9-60aa0b5a9bb4?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ]:
I recorded the video against the new agent.datasette.io [ https://substack.com/redirect/7c23b40e-9454-49ff-ba42-846587a8803d?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] live demo instance, which runs Datasette Agent against example databases including the classic global-power-plants [ https://substack.com/redirect/d6e76be8-7a33-4173-9ec7-c3e7593aa315?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] by WRI [ https://substack.com/redirect/491c20d1-eac2-4505-b3e2-3689ad93eae1?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ], and a copy of the Datasette backup [ https://substack.com/redirect/20026c9a-290b-458f-9a16-cf3ebd008378?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] of my blog.
The live demo runs on Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite [ https://substack.com/redirect/390391f9-1f99-4410-b46c-b9ad173e8890?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] - it’s cheap, fast and has no trouble writing SQLite queries.
A question I asked in the demo was:
when did Simon most recently see a pelican?
Which ran this SQL query [ https://substack.com/redirect/51c59c19-fa86-4a00-8a07-8ae4335715e6?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ]:
SELECT
  title, commentary, created
FROM
  blog_beat
WHERE
  beat_type = ‘sighting’
  AND (title LIKE ‘%pelican%’ OR commentary LIKE ‘%pelican%’)
ORDER BY
  created DESC
LIMIT
  5
And replied:
The most recent sighting of a pelican by Simon was recorded on May 20, 2026.
The observation included a California Brown Pelican, along with a Common Loon, Canada Goose, Striped Shore Crab, and a California Sea Lion.
Here’s that sighting on my blog [ https://substack.com/redirect/fa45fd14-eb63-4bfb-91d5-fcc0140c3d0b?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ], and the Markdown export [ https://substack.com/redirect/8b7aece6-bb40-4fe3-8b38-2bf00ad44b4e?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] of the full conversation transcript.
The plugins
My favorite feature of Datasette Agent is that, like the rest of Datasette, it’s extensible using plugins.
We’ve shipped three plugins so far:
datasette-agent-charts [ https://substack.com/redirect/a3b3e3cd-807f-4040-bc65-be2a2fd6142e?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ], shown in the video, adds charts to Datasette Agent, powered by Observable Plot [ https://substack.com/redirect/cca29ed9-9ac1-48f5-ac0c-95a95e6db694?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ].
datasette-agent-openai-imagegen [ https://substack.com/redirect/00075a65-7b2d-4e9f-9982-bd0b5ca497b8?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] adds an image generation tool to Datasette Agent using ChatGPT Images 2.0 [ https://substack.com/redirect/cf34c88b-b97f-478a-ba83-90a63dafdbca?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ].
datasette-agent-sprites [ https://substack.com/redirect/11e9595b-bdef-4d3b-acb5-c887afd2bbf8?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] provides tools for executing code in a Fly Sprites [ https://substack.com/redirect/9b46acff-9f8f-4d1a-bea0-03845308d168?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] persistent sandbox.
Building plugins is really fun. I have a bunch more prototypes that aren’t quite alpha-quality yet.
Claude Code and OpenAI Codex are both proving excellent at writing plugins - just point them at a checkout of the datasette-agent repo [ https://substack.com/redirect/60acfc75-af7a-4857-b0f4-ac45e2e2cbaa?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] for reference and tell them what you want to build!
Running it against local models
I’ve also been having fun running the new plugin against local models. Here’s a uv one-liner to run the plugin against gemma-4-26b-a4b [ https://substack.com/redirect/02ee969c-8910-4708-aef7-685a27eb27b1?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] in LM Studio [ https://substack.com/redirect/c6f0ffa8-647d-4b32-bce5-3deb7f63bc51?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] on a Mac:
uvx --prerelease=allow \
  --with datasette-agent --with llm-lmstudio \
  datasette --internal internal.db --root \
  -s plugins.datasette-llm.default_model lmstudio/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b \
  data.db
Datasette Agent needs reliable tool calls and the ability for a model to produce SQL queries that run against SQLite. The open weight models released in the past six months are increasingly able to handle that.
What’s next
Datasette Agent opens up so many opportunities for the LLM and Datasette ecosystem in general.
It’s already informed the major LLM 0.32a0 refactor [ https://substack.com/redirect/8e13391f-fe64-462d-b874-b7ad9dbfd748?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] which I’m nearly ready to roll into a stable release, maybe with some additional “LLM agent” abstractions extracte from Datasette Agent itself.
I’ve been exploring my own take on the Claude Artifacts, which is shaping up nicely as a plugin.
I’m excited to use Datasette Agent to build my own Claw [ https://substack.com/redirect/586979ff-b216-49c7-ab87-ff6294e4085a?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCyFYN9tX8izo2S8jR1GNw ] - a personal AI assistant built around data imported from different parts of my digital life, which is a neat excuse to revisit my older Dogsheep [ https://substack.com/redirect/22bc1690-c4a7-4454-8ddb-a8a03531549d?j=eyJ1IjoiOGZ6aG43In0.MEdLiOcZRUc_N3oL6SgEUFCy

## Phill Agnew — The odd reason why people love Matcha lattes | Nudge Newsletter

_From: `[email]` · 2026-05-22T08:46:23+00:00_

*******************
New and Safe Effect
*******************

​Read online ( https://a7046da1.click.kit-mail3.com/75u6wn862lu8h67xv57bzhw4nw65gbnho3708/3ohphkh3lnnr95sr/aHR0cHM6Ly9udWRnZS5raXQuY29tL3Byb2ZpbGU= )​

In the early 1970s an ambitious young director released his film THX 1138.

​
The concept went against many of the typical Hollywood storylines at the time.

Set in a dystopian future where sex is outlawed and drug-taking is mandatory, the film was wildly different from what audiences were used to.

The film was also a massive flop.

Despite the a-list cast and big marketing budget, few watched it. The young director was discouraged and almost gave up until he read The Hero With A Thousand Faces.

​
Joseph Campbell's book reveals how different cultures share remarkably similar hero stories.

He suggests that the innate human experience leads all of us to prefer surprisingly similar tales. For example:

* Goodies vs baddies
* Coming of age
* David vs goliath

Campbell encourages writers to develop new concepts on familiar and safe themes.

It's now termed the new and safe effect, or NaS effect.

The young director took this advice onboard and created a film you've probably heard of.

​
George Lucas isn't the first director to successfully apply NaS. In fact, marketers regularly do the same.

In 2013, researchers Shapiro and Nielsen asked dozens of participants to review hundreds of ads¹.

One group was shown the same jam ad for Druk every 50 ads.

The other group was shown almost the same ad, but with the logo moved to different corners.

​
All the participants preferred the jam if they'd seen it before (we prefer familiar things).

But those participants who saw slightly different versions liked it even more (we prefer new things that are familiar).

We see this in food trends.

NaS = chicken tikka, avocado on toast, matcha latte, and kombucha. No NaS = matcha milk tofu
Matcha lattes became insanely popular because they combined a new ingredient (matcha) with something safe and familiar (a latte).

Matcha milk tofu will never catch on, because both ingredients (tofu and matcha) are too new and unfamiliar.

But how can you apply this effect?

You're not developing food trends or producing Hollywood movies.

But you're probably writing headlines. Email subject lines, blog headers, and presentation titles.

In 2013² three researchers studied what made a good title.

Over several months, they posted the same meme on Reddit dozens of times but tweaked the title.

​
This allowed them to pinpoint which titles drove the highest engagement.

Their takeaway proved how important the NaS effect is.

A good headline is “not overly familiar, but rather familiar enough; a welcome surprise expressed in the vernacular of its intended audience.”
​

The takeaway is simple.

The best products, movies, headlines, and even ads combine two elements.

They're novel and new. But also familiar and safe.

Do you agree?

​

P.S. This newsletter is a trimmed-down version of the talk I gave at Creator Day ( https://a7046da1.click.kit-mail3.com/75u6wn862lu8h67xv57bzhw4nw65gbnho3708/n2hohvhvpkkg5zc6/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY3JlYXRvcmRheS51ay8= ) last week. The next one is the 6th of May 2027.

## Those who blindly accept AI answers are losing their confidence

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a03eea92-c02d-4dff-a931-0a748d62c293/AI_blindly.png?t=1779414084)
Caption: 

### The news

A recent [article in TIME explores](https://time.com/article/2026/04/15/how-ai-use-affects-confidence-thinking-study/) a new [peer-reviewed study published in Technology, Mind, and Behavior](https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/releases/tmb-tmb0000191.pdf). In the study, 1,923 adults used AI tools to complete simulated workplace tasks like drafting a salary negotiation plan, interpreting ambiguous data, and making strategic decisions. 

The people who accepted AI's first response and moved on reported lower confidence in their own reasoning and a weaker sense of ownership over their ideas. People who pushed back, edited, and questioned reported the opposite.

### What it means for marketers

* Study author Sarah Baldeo described a “self-confidence loop”: people who already feel uncertain about their abilities are more likely to defer to AI, and deferring deepens that uncertainty. Higher confidence makes for healthier AI use, and vice versa.

* Senior workers were more likely to override AI outputs and reported higher confidence than their junior counterparts. The more you know, the easier it is to push back.

* The practical advice from both Baldeo and Wharton professor Ethan Mollick: be intentional about which tasks you actually want to do yourself. Sometimes the less efficient path is worth it. 

“If the AI solves the problem for you, you don't think and you don't learn.” Ethan Mollick, Associate Professor at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania“The brands that act like publishers are going to win AI search”

## RIP Spirit Airlines. Here’s what led to its demise…

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7b10e180-9d24-4ffd-8f37-f306a84dbe35/Spirit.png?t=1779414094)
Caption: 

### The news

Budget airline Spirit [shut down in early May](https://www.forbes.com/sites/rogerdooley/2026/05/05/why-spirit-airlines-failed-and-united-is-winning-customer-experience-matters/?ss=cmo-network). Its second bankruptcy ended without a buyer, without a federal rescue, and without any other way to keep flying. About 17,000 employees lost their jobs.

The same week, the _Wall Street Journal_ ran a [profile of United CEO Scott Kirby](https://www.wsj.com/business/airlines/united-airlines-ceo-scott-kirby-delta-american-11621d97?st=bMQFFL&reflink=desktopwebshare_permalink) calling United's premium-experience strategy a “huge bet” that's paying off. Last year, Delta and United together captured more than 90% of U.S. airline industry profits.

### What it means for marketers

* Spirit's model was a pure price play, and it had no insulation when costs moved against them. When jet fuel prices recently spiked, larger carriers absorbed the hit by raising fares on premium products customers actually wanted. Spirit had nothing to raise.

* United did the opposite of Spirit on almost every dimension: they put seatback screens back on planes, cut a Starlink deal for real in-flight Wi-Fi, built a tool called ConnectionSaver that holds flights for passengers running between gates. They focused on customer experience at every moment.

* When your customers tolerate you rather than choose you, the relationship is fragile from day one. For B2B marketers, the version of this is a product that wins on feature count but loses on experience. Cheaper doesn't build loyalty.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/74d71b14-6bfd-4473-a681-67758447e1f8/0522_Article_Photo_1.png?t=1779464917)
Caption: Jenny Hoyos' new YouTube rebrand includes posting at least 20 videos a day / [Jenny Hoyos](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WZSPOUzn9SE)

Short-form creator [Jenny Hoyos](https://www.youtube.com/@JennyHoyos/featured) recently rebranded her 11M-subscriber challenge YouTube channel—with a new look (no glasses, hair down) and more personal content. 

With the rebrand, Hoyos increased her posting **from once a day to 20–100 videos per day, **publishing on the hour, every hour. The result: _nearly 1 billion views in a single month_ and deeper audience engagement.

**Here’s how she did it → **Hoyos works with a team of five (two ideators, two editors, and a strategist). She films during the day, sends footage to her editors and strategist, reviews at night, and schedules videos to publish hourly from midnight.

**“**==My goal is at least 20 new pieces of content, but if I run out, then I'll repurpose,” Hoyos told us. “I also have a server with all my videos and existing footage that my team goes through and picks out BTS.” ==

**Why post so much? **To build audience connection. In building up to 9M subscribers, Hoyos went viral multiple times but felt disconnected from her audience.

 "I was getting views and gaining subscribers and making money, but there was something that just felt missing," Hoyos said.

So she started including more of her personal life: [getting ready](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/LoW0-3SM040) for the day, letting viewers into her [friend group](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/AFjy3nAQL1E), and a [will-they-won't-they](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/veFzRCwl5e8) storyline with her best friend.

**What she found: **Weaving personal storylines into her content created a curiosity gap that spanned her entire channel, not just a single video. 

"People wouldn't just watch one video—they would watch several because they wanted to follow along with a storyline," Hoyos said. 

**And with hourly posting, the total time her audience spent with her content shot up. ** “At that point, they're probably logging more time than they are with some long-form creators,” Hoyos said.

**Playing the long game with Shorts: **When Hoyos first shifted her content style in November, views fell from 1 million to 50K per video. She kept going, likening her new content to a home renovation: "For the house to get prettier, it has to get uglier first."

Caption: CapCut will be integrated into the Google Gemini app / [CapCut](https://x.com/capcutapp/status/2057340757896216641?s=20)

Yesterday, ByteDance (TikTok’s parent company) announced that its free editing software CapCut would soon [be integrated](https://x.com/capcutapp/status/2057340757896216641?s=46) into the Google Gemini app—giving users the ability to edit videos and images directly in the LLM.

This move follows a partnership between CapCut and Google [last summer](https://www.androidauthority.com/google-photos-capcut-button-apk-teardown-3580017/), where Google Photos installed an “Edit in CapCut” button.

**Why it matters: **CapCut is one of the most popular free mobile video editing tools, with over [730 million](https://a16z.com/100-gen-ai-apps-6/) monthly active users. By inking one of its largest distribution deals with Google Gemini, CapCut can potentially rival other editing services from companies like Adobe and Apple. 

**Worth noting:** Google rolled out a beta version of its own free video software, YouTube Create, last December—but it has significantly fewer users than CapCut.

## @benradack
How to build a TRUE retargeting campaign on Meta.

If you want to test retargeting properly (instead of trusting Meta to do it inside your prospecting), here's the exact setup.

**Step 1: Use the OLD audience setting**

Click "Further Limit Your Audience" instead of using audience suggestions. Audience suggestions just go broad with some direction. You want controlled audiences, not Meta's interpretation.

**Step 2: Set your custom audiences down the funnel**

→ Checkouts last 90 days
→ Add to carts last 90 days
→ Website visitors last 90 days

**Step 3: Exclude all existing customers**

→ Pixel based purchasers
→ Email list

You want people who almost bought. Not people who already did.

**A few notes:**

I don't include people who just engaged with posts. Social engagement doesn't mean purchase intent. I only want to retarget people who showed real interest (visited the site, added to cart, started checkout).

You could technically set the audience window to 180 days. Doesn't matter much. Meta prioritizes recent high intent actions anyway.

**Why this matters:**

Most "retargeting" campaigns aren't actually retargeting. They use audience suggestions which means Meta goes broad and treats your warm audience as a hint, not a rule.

This setup forces Meta to ONLY target people who already interacted with your funnel.

True warm traffic. Not "kinda warm maybe" traffic.

## @benradack
Your ad says one thing. Your landing page says something else. The person bounces.

This is one of the most common conversion killers and most brands don't even realize they're doing it.

Here's the typical mismatch:

→ Ad: "Stop back pain while you sleep"
→ Landing page headline: "Premium ergonomic pillows"

The message breaks. Trust breaks. They leave.

The fix is congruency. Whatever your ad promises, your landing page needs to deliver immediately.

→ If the ad says "Stop back pain while you sleep" the LP should say "Stop back pain while you sleep"
→ Not "Premium ergonomic pillows"

A few examples of how to match the angle:

→ Fear based ad? LP should address the consequences of inaction
→ Aspirational ad? LP should focus on the transformation
→ Problem solver ad? LP should lead with that exact problem

Why this matters.

People bounce in seconds. If they don't immediately see what the ad promised, they assume something is off and leave. Even a second or two of confusion tanks your conversion rate.

Easiest CRO win in your account. Match the angle of every ad to the headline of every landing page. Stop sending traffic to generic product pages and expecting them to convert.

## @benradack
Your scaling campaign is probably top heavy and you don't even know it.

The fix is to separate your winners into two ad sets instead of putting them all in one.

→ Ad set 1: Old winners (historical proven ads)
→ Ad set 2: Newly tested winners with min and max spend limits

Why this matters.

If you put all your winners in one ad set, the old ads with the most engagement will suck up all the spend. When they fatigue (and they will), your account crashes because there's no depth behind them.

There's also a second problem. When you drop a new ad into a scaling ad set, sometimes Meta dumps all the budget into the new ad. But because the ad is new, it still takes 3-4 days to optimize and get the CPA down. That's 3-4 days of bad performance eating your budget.

The fix.

→ Min spend limit on the new ads ad set at 3-4x your average CPA
→ Max spend limit at 3-4x your min spend

This forces Meta to deliver budget into your new ads but caps how much damage they can do while they're learning.

As that ad set proves itself, raise the max spend limit. Eventually remove it entirely.

What this gets you:

→ Old winners keep producing without getting buried by new ads
→ New winners get forced spend but can't blow up the account
→ The account stays resilient when something fatigues

Two ad sets. Min and max spend limits. Controlled scale.
